state.initial_idea: Azure SQL Database exporter to AWS RDS SQL Server. DRY, minimal dependencies, self-bootstrapping, Linux/bash CLI, terabyte-scale, converts Azure-specific SQL features to AWS RDS compatible equivalents. User also wants: $ralplan for REST-to-CLI migration plan, $ralph for persistent implementation, $team 3:executor for parallel frontend/backend/data layer build.

answers.Q1: B — tool exposes both REST API (backend control) and Linux CLI (frontend). API keeps backend running uninterrupted; CLI controls it.
answers.Q2: C+D — full migration (schema+data+jobs+logins where compatible) plus incremental sync via external tools if possible.
answers.Q3: Open — agent to recommend language with fewest deps and easiest maintenance.

round3_answers.Q10: C+D — REST API polling + CLI STDOUT progress + SQLite job-log persistence across restarts.
round3_answers.Q11: B — skip SQL Agent jobs entirely.
round3_answers.Q12: D — fully user-configurable sync schedule per database profile, set dynamically via input.

round2_answers.Q5: Python 3 + pyodbc + apscheduler approved. Add real-time migration status/progress reporting for multi-step processes.
round2_answers.Q6: Direct TCP endpoints. Config file OR interactive questionnaire-style setup wizard. Per-server profiles.
round2_answers.Q7: Tool runs on its own AWS/Azure instance to minimise data transfer costs. Output: compressed SQL files (.sql.gz) AND BACPAC. Both supported, flag-controlled.
round2_answers.Q8: C — unit tests + integration tests. Integration tests gated behind flag, runnable once real instances are available.
round2_answers.Q9: Drop Elastic Query, Drop Stretch DB, Skip OPENROWSET, Strip Azure Key Vault refs (keep column encryption skeleton), Drop geo-replication/failover groups. Keep RLS, temporal tables, JSON functions.
